content.text:
I've submitted the campaign, picking **index 74** (Bi 0.07, Cu 0.54, V 0.39) as the best composition, with a photocurrent of **1.7×10⁻⁷ A**.

I used all 3 merit measurements:

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 19 | 0.16 / 0.27 / 0.57 | 0 A |
| 73 | 0.09 / 0.48 / 0.44 | 1.2×10⁻⁷ A |
| 74 | 0.07 / 0.54 / 0.39 | 1.7×10⁻⁷ A |

**Why these three:** the light is 2.06 eV, below the ~2.4 eV band gap of BiVO₄, so BiVO₄ can't absorb it. Any photocurrent should come from copper vanadates, which have narrower gaps. The measurements fit this: the V-rich sample gave nothing, and photocurrent went up as Cu increased. Index 74 is the most Cu-rich candidate in the vanadate-rich part of the library, with a Cu:V ratio close to Cu₃V₂O₈.

**Limits:**
- Three measurements cover very little of a 137-composition library, so I can't say 74 is the best one there.
- I didn't measure the low-V, Cu–Bi-rich region (indices 76–136). I left it out because it's probably mostly CuBi₂O₄/CuO, which are poor photoanodes, but I didn't test that.
- I spent none of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phase assignments are chemical reasoning and weren't checked.
- The list of known phases was too large to return, so I didn't review it.
